info.name: Tamagotchi Go - Game Workflows
info.description:
End-to-end game workflows that cross every service of Tamagotchi Go through the API Gateway (Lab 2).

| Folder | Story | Services |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Gateway entry and authorization | Gateway, User Management, Tamagotchi, Battle |
| 1 | Onboarding: players, package and pets | User Management, Package Registry, Tamagotchi, Notification |

Run the folders in order with the Collection Runner. Every run creates fresh players, so it can be
repeated on the same stack. Setup, required local values and Lab 2 coverage are in
`docs/game-workflows.md`. Never export or commit populated secrets or tokens.

exec: // One correlation id per call: the gateway forwards it and the services pass it on to every
// service-to-service call, so a whole workflow step can be traced in the logs.
// Trace any step with: docker compose logs api-gateway | grep <correlation id>

item.name: 0. Gateway entry and authorization
item.description:
**Lab 2 grades 6, 9 and 10.** The API Gateway is the only door into the system: it validates bearer
tokens against the User Management JWKS, removes `Authorization` and any identity headers the caller
sent, and forwards a verified identity (`X-Caller-Kind`, `X-User-ID` or `X-Service-Name`) instead.

Runs on its own: it registers a throwaway "probe" player. The service-token checks need
`battleClientSecret`.

request.description: Gateway-owned probe. 503 NOT_READY means it has not fetched the signing keys yet.

item.name: 1. Onboarding: players, package and pets
item.description:
**Services:** User Management, Package Registry, Tamagotchi, Notification, all through the gateway.

Three players (Alice, Bob, Carol) register without a package. Alice publishes her own game package
with statistics and battle boosts, everyone joins it, and each player hatches a primary Tamagotchi.
Service-to-service calls in this folder:
`User Management → Package Registry` (registration) and `Tamagotchi → Package Registry` (stat validation).

request.description: Public operation. Registration no longer needs a package, so a clean deployment can bootstrap itself.
